title: Sweeteners
subtitle: Not sugar. But not neutral either.
description: Non-sugar sweeteners add sweetness without calories. They appear in products marketed as 'light', 'zero' or 'diet'. BOTIA flags them because their long-term effects are under active scientific review.
why_body: WHO (2023) advises against using non-sugar sweeteners for weight control. Long-term use has been associated with increased risk of type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and mortality. They are authorised — but the science is not settled.
what_body: BOTIA detects ingredients classified as non-sugar sweeteners: aspartame (E951), acesulfame K (E950), sucralose (E955), saccharin (E954), cyclamates (E952), stevia (E960), and sugar alcohols such as sorbitol, maltitol, xylitol and erythritol. Each has a different profile — BOTIA flags their presence so you can decide.
can_1: Detect non-sugar sweeteners declared on the label.
can_2: Flag sugar alcohols that may cause digestive effects in large quantities.
can_3: Signal when a 'sugar-free' product contains multiple sweeteners.
cannot_1: Tell you whether sweeteners are safe for you personally.
cannot_2: Quantify your daily sweetener intake or cumulative exposure.
closing: If you are monitoring sweetener intake, check both the ingredient list and the nutrition label.
source_note: WHO Guideline: Use of non-sugar sweeteners (2023) · EFSA re-evaluation of sweeteners (ongoing)
